question: Is ultra-processed food bad for you?

say: You eat breakfast from a box, lunch from a wrapper and dinner from a bag, then blame your willpower.
Let's look at the food instead.
For most of history, people cooked meals from things that grew, swam or walked.
Ultra-processed food is made in factories from parts of foods and additives, like packaged snacks and fizzy drinks.
In a hospital study, twenty adults ate as much as they wanted: two weeks of ultra-processed meals, and two weeks of fresh meals with the same nutrients on offer.
On the packaged food, they ate about five hundred extra calories a day and gained almost a kilo.
They were the same people, with the same willpower.
In a newer trial, both diets followed healthy eating advice, and people lost only about half as much weight on the ultra-processed one.
So cook from food that still looks like what it came from, and make packaged snacks, sugary drinks and processed meat the exception.
A potato is food. A potato-flavoured snack is a hobby.
If you take medicine for diabetes or your heart, better food works with it, not instead of it.
Let's get you back to factory settings.

dicken2025: Dicken SJ et al. Ultraprocessed or minimally processed diets following healthy dietary guidelines on weight and cardiometabolic health: a randomized, crossover trial (UPDATE). Nature Medicine 2025: 55 adults in England, two 8-week diets both following the UK Eatwell Guide; weight fell 2.06% on minimally processed food and 1.05% on ultra-processed food (difference 1.01 percentage points, P = 0.024)
santefr: Santé publique France via sante.fr (updated 1 Oct 2026): reduce "Les boissons sucrées, les aliments gras, sucrés, salés et ultra-transformés"; increase "Le fait maison"
canada: Health Canada, Canada's Dietary Guidelines, Appendix A (updated 23 Mar 2026): "Limit highly processed foods. If you choose these foods, eat them less often."
fang2024: Fang Z et al. Association of ultra-processed food consumption with all cause and cause specific mortality: population based cohort study. BMJ 2024;385:e078476: 74,563 women and 39,501 men followed about three decades; highest vs lowest intake 4% higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.04, 1.01 to 1.07); the link was driven by meat, poultry and seafood based ready-to-eat products and sugar-sweetened and artificially sweetened drinks, among others; better diet quality was linked to lower mortality at every level of ultra-processed intake
lane2024: Lane MM et al. Ultra-processed food exposure and adverse health outcomes: umbrella review of epidemiological meta-analyses. BMJ 2024;384:e077310: 45 pooled analyses, 9,888,373 participants, all observational; definition of ultra-processed foods ("Ready to eat products, including packaged snacks, carbonated soft drinks, instant noodles, and ready-made meals", "industrial formulations primarily composed of chemically modified substances extracted from foods, along with additives"); higher exposure linked to cardiovascular disease mortality, type 2 diabetes, all-cause mortality, common mental disorders (mostly low or very low certainty)
hall2019: Hall KD et al. Ultra-processed diets cause excess calorie intake and weight gain: an inpatient randomized controlled trial of ad libitum food intake. Cell Metab 2019;30:67-77: 20 adults on a metabolic ward for 4 weeks, 2 weeks ultra-processed and 2 weeks unprocessed, meals with matched nutritional profiles on offer, eating as much as they liked; energy intake 508 kcal a day greater on the ultra-processed diet; gained 0.9 kg on ultra-processed, lost 0.9 kg on unprocessed; meals eaten faster on ultra-processed
